briefFidelity: FAIL, and the failure is on the brief's own explicit negative constraints, not on taste. The brief says 'hairline linework', 'nothing heavy, nothing solid, NO FILLED MASS ANYWHERE', and 'the contrast kept low so the lines read as thread rather than as structure'. Before I had read a word of it I described the material, unprompted, as 'flat, hard-edged rectangular bars or planks... semi-transparent so where bars cross they accumulate into brighter mass', and reached for the words 'scaffolding' and 'a pile of milled lumber'. I named the exact thing the brief forbids and I used the exact noun the brief rules out. The filled mass is not incidental, it is the dominant visual event: 1366079 is a single solid unbroken ivory hexagonal PLATE at the centre; 1310661 is a near-featureless solid white disc in all three states; 1203347 under stress is an unbroken ivory plateau; 1991107 and 1243682 both saturate to flat cream fields. Contrast is not low, it is the widest the medium offers -- blown-out bone white against a near-black ground -- so the marks read as structure, which is precisely the reading the brief writes the constraint to prevent. Genuine hairline thread does exist, in 1475115, 1733538, 1835793 and 1561509, but as a minority accent whiskering off a heavy filled core, not as the material of the work. This is a frost-crystal / shattered-scaffolding collection built from heavy slats. It is not FILIGREE.
composition: Strong on its own terms and the best axis here. Every token has a real focal hierarchy -- a bright centre-weighted core with radial arms -- and it is plainly deliberate rather than an even field of incident. The frame is used hard: 1203347 (left edge), 1310661 (bottom), 1985692 (right) and the 512 single all run bars flush off all four borders, so nothing floats in a polite margin. The defect is that on 1203347 (stress), 1310661 (all three states), 1366079 and 1991107 the focal point is the LEAST informative region of the picture: accumulated alpha saturates to a flat ivory plateau with no interior left, so the eye is led to a blank. 1835793 and 1733538 show what is being lost, because they hold their interior tracery. And 'provisional, as though it could be disturbed' is the opposite of what a centre-saturated plateau communicates -- these read as immovable.
collectionCoherence: Passes comfortably, arguably too well. All twelve share the slat primitive, near six-fold radial symmetry, centre-weighted mass, the bone-and-slate-on-near-black palette, and the decision to clip at every border. Even the outliers stay inside the family: 1446330 is sparse and scattered but is recognisably the same figure thinned out, and 1561509 is dark and grainy but is the same rosette in negative. Laid out together, 1203347, 1243682, 1475115, 1733538, 1835793 and 1991107 read as siblings at a glance. This is a collection, not a folder. The coherence is real -- it is simply the coherence of a different project than the one commissioned.
palette: Chosen and consistent -- warm bone/ivory against cool slate blue-grey on a near-black slate ground, and the ground supports rather than competes; it stays quiet in the corners of 1446330 and 1561509 where the most of it shows. But the contrast RANGE is the direct opposite of what was asked. The brief wants it 'kept low so the lines read as thread'; this runs from about black to full ivory, and the top of the range is not doing work because it is clipped -- 1203347, 1310661, 1366079 and 1991107 blow out to a flat plateau, so the brightest values carry no information at all. 1283437 and 1985692 invert the relationship into dark lattice over a pale field, which is the most controlled colour in the set and shows the palette can behave; 1561509 is the only token where the low-contrast, cool, provisional feel the brief describes is actually achieved.
seedVariation: Middling. There is genuine range -- 1446330 (sparse, drifting, mostly dark ground), 1561509 (charcoal blocks and a tight grainy core), 1366079 (one solid hexagonal plate), and 1985692 and 1283437 (dark slate lattice drawn over a pale field, inverting the value logic of the rest) are each individual works. Against that, 1203347, 1243682, 1475115, 1733538, 1835793 and 1991107 -- half the set -- are near-siblings separated only by how fine the fringe is. Neither failure mode is fatal on its own. The real finding is that the brief names the variation axes as 'the symmetry of the figure and how far its threads extend', and neither is what varies: all twelve read as essentially six-fold (1733538 and 1835793 push slightly higher-order and that is the whole of it), and reach is pinned at maximum because eleven of twelve clip the frame. What actually varies is density and value, which the brief never asked for.
thumbnailSurvival: The silhouette survives completely -- at 120px every one of the twelve still reads as a radial rosette on black and the six-fold geometry is still obvious, which is more than most work manages. But it survives as the wrong object. The first thing to die at 120 is the hairline thread the brief makes central: the needles in 1475115, 1733538, 1835793 and 1561509 collapse into an undifferentiated cream haze, and the interior of 1203347's hexagonal ring becomes a grey smudge. What survives is exactly the filled mass the brief forbids. Individuality holds for 1366079 (solid disc), 1446330 (sparse), 1561509 (dark), 1283437 and 1985692 (dark lattice over pale); 1203347, 1243682, 1475115, 1733538, 1835793 and 1991107 converge into one repeated cream stamp. So this work passes the browse-size test by virtue of the single property that disqualifies it.
marketResponse: Visible, and wrong on both counts the brief specifies. The brief asks that the figure's REACH expand and contract -- 'it opens out in recovery and draws in under stress' -- and that 'the change must be carried by the geometry rather than by weight'. Of the four seeds shown in state, reach visibly moves on exactly one, 1243682, and it moves BACKWARDS: its stress frame swells larger and soft-edged than neutral, and its recovery frame contracts to a tight compact rosette smaller than neutral. On the other three the carrier is weight and value, the forbidden mechanism: 1283437 goes pale-dominant to slate-dominant to darkest-of-all in recovery, so its recovery is heavier than its stress and the three do not order into any narrative; 1310661 changes only by being veiled with crossing slate bars under stress; and 1203347's hollow hexagonal centre FILLS IN SOLID under stress, which is added mass, the one thing the brief says must exist nowhere. The one state change I found genuinely beautiful, 1203347's recovery into a dotted filigree core, is a texture change, not a reach change.
tokenIdentity: Passes cleanly, and it is the second-strongest axis. Same seed across three states stays recognisably one token: 1203347 keeps its hexagonal-ring family and its bar rhythm through all three; 1243682 keeps its dark hexagonal core as a signature even as the surrounding figure swells and contracts; 1310661 keeps its ivory disc; 1283437 swings furthest -- pale field with slate lattice becomes slate-dominant -- but the underlying lattice geometry and the hexagram voids persist, so it reads as the same object under different light rather than a replacement. Nothing here becomes a different work under drawdown.
artifacts: No collisions into mush, no vanishing strokes, no shape severed by the viewBox in a way that reads as error; edges are clean throughout. Bars terminate flush at the border on essentially every token (1203347 left, 1310661 bottom, 1985692 right, the 512 single on all four), and because it is that consistent I read it as a deliberate crop rather than clipping. Two real defects. First, alpha saturation: 1203347 (stress), 1310661 (all states), 1366079 and 1991107 accumulate to a flat blown-out ivory plateau that destroys interior information, and 1835793 and 1733538 prove it is avoidable. Second, orphaned marks: isolated single bars sitting alone in the black at 1243682's upper-left and 1985692's upper-right, and throughout 1446330, which read as deliberate scatter at 256 and as dust on the lens at 120.
reasoning: I wrote my description before opening the brief, and the description and the brief describe two different artworks. Unprompted I called the material 'flat, hard-edged rectangular planks' that 'accumulate into brighter mass', and reached for 'scaffolding' and 'milled lumber'; the brief asks for hairline thread, low contrast, and states 'nothing heavy, nothing solid, no filled mass anywhere' and that the marks must read 'as thread rather than as structure'. I independently used the disqualifying word. That is not a near miss or a matter of degree: filled mass is the dominant visual event of the collection -- 1366079's solid hexagonal plate, 1310661's featureless white disc, 1203347's stress plateau -- and the contrast is at maximum where the brief asks for it to be minimal. The second independent failure is the market axis: the brief commissions expansion and contraction of reach carried by geometry, and what ships is modulation of weight and value on 1283437, 1310661 and 1203347, with the single seed whose reach does move, 1243682, moving the wrong way -- swelling under stress and contracting in recovery. On its own terms this is accomplished, coherent work that survives browse size better than most, and that is exactly why the gate exists: it survives at 120px because of the filled mass, the one property it was told not to have. REFUSE.
wouldChange: Change the material, not the styling. Make the dominant primitive an actual stroked hairline with no fill, and demote the filled slat to a rare accent or remove it -- the needles already present in 1475115, 1733538, 1835793 and 1561509 are the correct material and should be the whole of it. Compress the value range: bring the ivory down toward mid-grey and lift the ground off near-black so the figure reads as thread against dusk rather than as white structure against void, and hard-cap accumulated alpha so overlaps can never reach a flat plateau -- that single change fixes the blown centres of 1203347, 1310661, 1366079 and 1991107 and restores the interior that 1835793 shows is there. Re-map the market onto geometry: drive thread LENGTH and figure radius, so recovery pushes threads past the frame and stress pulls the figure in to leave a visible dark margin, and reverse the current mapping on 1243682, which is inverted. Stop 1283437 and 1310661 responding by darkening at all. Finally, make symmetry order a real seed variable, since the brief names it as a differentiator and all twelve currently read as six-fold; and vary reach across seeds instead of clipping the frame on eleven of twelve, which pins the brief's other stated variation axis at its maximum.
